basis: Monday's close · today's session news to 12:30 PM

stories.title: Wall Street gives back part of Monday's record AI rally; Dow holds up
stories.body: After Monday's best day since April 2025 (S&P 500 +4.73% to 7,237.17, Nasdaq +6.51% to 24,089.56, Dow +3.01% to 49,595.31), stocks split on Tuesday. As of 11:31 AM ET the Nasdaq was down 2.24% at 23,549 and the S&P 500 down 0.99% at 7,166, while the Dow was up 0.24% at 49,715 as chip stocks fell.
stories.why: A large gap-and-reverse sequence: Monday's +4.7% S&P 500 day is being partly retraced. Completed 1-hour closes, not intrahour swings, show whether the retracement holds or fades.

stories.title: Megacaps cool after Monday's broad rebound
stories.body: Tesla closed Monday at $385.46 (+11.46%), Meta at $597.60 (+6.55%), Alphabet's GOOG at $279.53 (+5.88%) and Amazon at $255.39 (+3.47%). Trefis found no stock-specific filing behind the Tesla and Meta gains, tying them to the broad rebound after Nvidia's leadership change; Tesla also began sending a major FSD software update Monday. By 12:00 PM ET Tuesday the four were down 1.6%–2.1%.
stories.why: Big Monday ranges in index heavyweights set wide reference levels; Tuesday's drift back inside them is visible on the completed hourly candles.

stories.title: Chip stocks slide as the AI trade comes under renewed pressure
stories.body: Semiconductors gave back part of Monday's surge (the SOXX chip ETF rose 13.63% Monday). At 12:00 PM ET Micron was down 11.74%, AMD 10.87%, Intel 9.30% and Broadcom 4.39%. Yahoo Finance said the declines came 'as the overall AI trade came under renewed pressure'; 24/7 Wall St. said Micron fell as Nvidia's pullback partially reversed Monday's AI chip rally, with SanDisk and SK Hynix down about 6%.
stories.why: High-beta names are posting double-digit swings in both directions on consecutive days; option premiums and hourly ranges are elevated accordingly.

stories.title: Energy shares firm after Monday's oil slide; banks flat
stories.body: Energy was the only S&P 500 sector besides staples to fall Monday (−1.06%) as WTI settled at $80.17 (−3.88%), its lowest close since Aug. 26, on rising supply. On Tuesday at 12:00 PM ET Chevron was up 1.65% and Exxon 1.10%, while JPMorgan was down 0.25% and Bank of America up 0.54%. Financials had gained 1.98% Monday.
stories.why: Energy and banks are moving on different drivers from tech this week (oil supply and Fed-hike pricing), which shows up as low correlation with QQQ on the hourly chart.

stories.title: Nvidia drops after its 31% Huang-return surge; SEC accounting probe still open
stories.body: Nvidia closed Monday at $165.05 (+31.48%), its best day since 2003, after its board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO. On Tuesday it was down 8.62% at 12:00 PM ET. Yahoo Finance said the pullback came 'as investors reassessed how much further the AI trade can run.' The Motley Fool noted Reuters' report that the SEC has opened a probe into Nvidia's accounting practices; the NYT described it as in its early stages. Huang is due before three House committees on Dec. 1.
stories.why: Two consecutive sessions with ranges above 9% leave the stock far from its moving averages; completed 1-hour closes matter more than headline prints while governance news is still unfolding.

stories.title: Gold and silver slip as Fed-hike bets firm before PCE
stories.body: Gold futures settled Monday at $3,634.30 (+3.38%), rebounding from a nearly 9% weekly drop, and silver at $42.98 (+4.74%). Kitco said spot gold was at $3,621.70 (−0.34%) and silver at $42.04 (−2.33%) around 8:37 AM ET Tuesday, pressured by a firm dollar and expectations of more Fed rate increases ahead of Wednesday's October PCE data. At 12:00 PM ET GLD was down 1.96% and SLV 5.29%.
stories.why: Metals ETFs are trading on rate expectations into a scheduled data release (PCE, 8:30 AM ET Wednesday), a known gap risk for positions held overnight.

stories.title: Iran orders Hormuz closed 'further'; Qatar's PM meets Vance and Rubio
stories.body: Euronews reported that Iran's army commander on Monday ordered the navy to close the Strait of Hormuz 'further day by day' until Iran's conditions are met; the IRGC said three tankers hit naval mines, which the Joint Maritime Information Centre called unconfirmed. Qatar's prime minister met Vice President Vance and Secretary of State Rubio separately in Washington to discuss restarting talks. WTI settled Monday at $80.17 (−3.88%) and Brent at $89.37 (−3.46%); Kitco put Brent at $89.10 and WTI at $79.97, both about −0.3%, in early European trading Tuesday.
stories.why: Headline-driven oil can gap between sessions; USO and OXY hourly closes show whether the market is treating the Hormuz news as supply risk.

stories.title: VIX ticks back up after Monday's 26% drop
stories.body: The VIX closed Monday at 26.62, down 25.84% from 35.89 as stocks rallied. The Weekend Spread put it at 28.28 (+6.2%) before Tuesday's open, with the Nasdaq volatility index VXN at 36.31 Monday and the VXN–VIX spread at 9.69.
stories.why: A VIX in the high 20s keeps implied volatility, and therefore option premiums and expected moves, well above normal levels.

stories.title: Fed-hike odds near certainty for December as Williams says the Fed has 'work to do'
stories.body: The 10-year Treasury yield ended Monday at 4.92%, the 2-year at 4.63% and the 30-year at 5.29% (Capp Notes). New York Fed President John Williams said inflation near 3.5% means the Fed has 'work to do'. CME FedWatch showed about a 98% chance of a 25 bp hike on Dec. 9, up from about 88% Friday; Kitco cited about 95% Tuesday. The Treasury auctions $70 billion of 5-year notes at 1:00 PM ET today.
stories.why: Rate-hike pricing is the macro backdrop for the tech pullback; yields and auction results can move index ETFs intraday.

stories.title: Asia rallies on Huang's return while Europe slips on chip and mining losses
stories.body: Trading Economics reported Japan's Nikkei 225 up 3.91% to 58,645 in a post-holiday session and Korea's KOSPI up 6.32% to 5,006 on renewed AI optimism, while the Shanghai Composite rose 0.27%; 24/7 Wall St. said the Hang Seng closed down 0.82%. In Europe the DAX fell 1.29% to 25,012 as Infineon dropped about 9%, and the FTSE 100 edged lower as miners led declines; the CAC 40 edged up 0.2%, helped by Sanofi's $41 billion Insmed deal.
stories.why: Overseas chip suppliers moved with Monday's US rally before Tuesday's US pullback, so overnight markets are lagging the US tape this week.

stories.title: Consumer confidence jumps to 103.3 in November
stories.body: The Conference Board's consumer confidence index rose 11.4 points to 103.3 in November from 91.9 in October, well above the 92.1 consensus cited by The Weekend Spread. The Present Situation Index rose to 132.8 and the Expectations Index to 83.6. The Rio Times reported that respondents saying jobs are 'plentiful' rose to 30.8% from 26.2%, and 12-month inflation expectations were 5.7%.
stories.why: A strong data surprise adds to the case the Fed is already pricing for a December hike; Wednesday's PCE release is the next scheduled data risk.

stories.title: Nvidia options hit a record and new long-dated puts pile up
stories.body: Current Logic reported that more than 11 million Nvidia options contracts traded Monday, the most for the stock in one day, just under 6.7 million of them calls. TheFly said Monday's total option volume was 82.7 million contracts, and the top new positions included 150k NVDA April-2027 80 puts, 138k January-2027 80 puts, 94k February-2027 120 puts and 83k January-2027 120 puts.
stories.why: Record volume and heavy open-interest changes show how much hedging and speculation is concentrated in one name; implied volatility stays elevated while it lasts. This is reported activity, not a signal.

stories.title: Ahead: PCE and GDP Wednesday, Thanksgiving close, Broadcom on Dec. 9
stories.body: Wednesday at 8:30 AM ET brings October PCE inflation, the second estimate of Q3 GDP, durable goods and weekly jobless claims, with the Fed's Beige Book at 2:00 PM ET (Kiplinger). US markets are closed Thursday for Thanksgiving and close at 1:00 PM ET Friday (The Weekend Spread). Jensen Huang faces three House committees on Dec. 1, the Fed meets Dec. 8–9, and Broadcom reports fiscal Q4 results after the close on Wednesday, Dec. 9, with its call at 5:00 PM ET.
stories.why: A holiday-shortened week with a heavy data morning before the break means fewer completed hourly candles and possible gaps around Thursday's closure.

es.Wall Street gives back part of Monday's: Wall Street devuelve parte del rally récord de IA del lunes; el Dow aguanta
es.After Monday's best day since April 2025: Tras el mejor día del lunes desde abril de 2025 (S&P 500 +4.73% a 7,237.17, Nasdaq +6.51% a 24,089.56, Dow +3.01% a 49,595.31), las bolsas se dividieron el martes. A las 11:31 AM ET el Nasdaq bajaba 2.24% a 23,549 y el S&P 500 bajaba 0.99% a 7,166, mientras el Dow subía 0.24% a 49,715 por la caída de los chips.
es.A large gap-and-reverse sequence: Monday: Una secuencia grande de gap y reversión: el día de +4.7% del S&P 500 del lunes se retrocede en parte. Los cierres completos de 1 hora, no los movimientos dentro de la hora, muestran si el retroceso se sostiene o se desvanece.
es.Megacaps cool after Monday's broad rebou: Las megacaps se enfrían tras el rebote amplio del lunes
es.Tesla closed Monday at $385.46 (+11.46%): Tesla cerró el lunes en $385.46 (+11.46%), Meta en $597.60 (+6.55%), GOOG de Alphabet en $279.53 (+5.88%) y Amazon en $255.39 (+3.47%). Trefis no encontró un reporte específico detrás de las subidas de Tesla y Meta y las vincula al rebote amplio tras el cambio de liderazgo en Nvidia; Tesla además empezó a enviar el lunes una actualización importante del software FSD. A las 12:00 PM ET del martes las cuatro bajaban entre 1.6% y 2.1%.
es.Big Monday ranges in index heavyweights: Los grandes rangos del lunes en los pesos pesados del índice dejan niveles de referencia amplios; el regreso del martes dentro de ellos se ve en las velas horarias completas.
es.Chip stocks slide as the AI trade comes: Los chips caen mientras el trade de IA vuelve a estar bajo presión
es.Semiconductors gave back part of Monday': Los semiconductores devolvieron parte del salto del lunes (el ETF de chips SOXX subió 13.63% el lunes). A las 12:00 PM ET Micron bajaba 11.74%, AMD 10.87%, Intel 9.30% y Broadcom 4.39%. Yahoo Finance dijo que las caídas llegaron 'mientras el trade de IA en general volvía a estar bajo presión'; 24/7 Wall St. dijo que Micron cayó porque el retroceso de Nvidia revirtió en parte el rally de chips de IA del lunes, con SanDisk y SK Hynix bajando cerca de 6%.
es.High-beta names are posting double-digit: Los nombres de beta alta registran movimientos de dos dígitos en ambas direcciones en días consecutivos; las primas de opciones y los rangos horarios están elevados en consecuencia.

El martes a las 12:00 PM ET Chevron subía 1.65% y Exxon 1.10%, mientras JPMorgan bajaba 0.25% y Bank of America subía 0.54%. Financieras habían ganado 1.98% el lunes.
es.Energy and banks are moving on different: Energía y bancos se mueven esta semana por factores distintos a la tecnología (oferta de petróleo y expectativas de alza de la Fed), lo que se ve como baja correlación con QQQ en el gráfico horario.
es.Nvidia drops after its 31% Huang-return: Nvidia cae tras subir 31% por el regreso de Huang; sigue abierta la investigación contable de la SEC
es.Nvidia closed Monday at $165.05 (+31.48%: Nvidia cerró el lunes en $165.05 (+31.48%), su mejor día desde 2003, después de que su junta reinstalara por unanimidad a Jensen Huang como CEO. El martes bajaba 8.62% a las 12:00 PM ET. Yahoo Finance dijo que el retroceso llegó 'mientras los inversionistas reevaluaban cuánto más puede correr el trade de IA'. The Motley Fool citó el reporte de Reuters de que la SEC abrió una investigación sobre las prácticas contables de Nvidia; el NYT la describió como en etapa inicial. Huang debe comparecer ante tres comités de la Cámara el 1 de diciembre.
